description: The Agents escape the Museum with the key incantation and formulate the D-Day Plan; at the hearing, reciting the incantation publicly exposes Brant's Nazi identity; Labinski publicly shoots Landa; the Agents are awarded medals and transferred to the specialized Providence Team for researching anomalous phenomena, embarking on a new journey

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: A new story begins, have a pleasant journey!

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: After escaping from the Museum, you fled in a panic in journalist Margaret's vehicle. Margaret dropped you off at an intersection as requested.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Andrew is still shaken. The time in the car has calmed him slightly, but his right hand remains glued to the pistol in his pocket.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Immediately tries to open the case upon getting in the car to check if our goods are inside.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Inside is a handwritten book with a black cover. On the cover is a line of Russian words written in red pigment.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Harting is still dead. We didn't manage to save him in time. But it seems he managed to plant some kind of mark on Heim during the soul contact of the spellcasting process."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player4>'s Russian check result:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You recognize this word as "Black Book of the Old World," and as if by fate, on the very first page you randomly flip to, you discover that spell—the spell you need.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Found the spell."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Finally." David finally lets out a sigh of relief.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "You found it? That's wonderful!" Andrew's spirits lift greatly, and his fingers become much more flexible. He leans his head over, though he doesn't recognize anything.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: David also leans over, intending to learn it.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Let's learn it quickly."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player5>'s Russian check result:

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Memorize the spell and try to recite it.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Labinski learns that line of mysterious spell phonetically transcribed in Slavic letters.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Alison lets out a long sigh. After being highly tense for several days, she finally gets some relaxation, and her body can't help but feel a bit weak.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're good at quite a few things.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Alison takes a look too.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player6>'s Russian check result:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: For some reason, you find this line of the spell utterly disgusting. Combined with the previous experiences, you lean against the wall and vomit profusely.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Ugh..." Alison leans against the wall and vomits up her entire lunch.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Are you okay, Alison?" David pats her back.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Andrew hands her a tissue while recalling what he has learned in his mind.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We have the spell, the chain of evidence is complete. Let's find a place to report to the boss first."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Now we have the spell and the previous files, that old bastard Brant can't escape."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "I'm okay. Maybe it's because I've experienced too many strange things these past few days." Alison cleans up briefly.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Call the boss." David looks for a phone booth.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You find a random public phone booth.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: David dials Turner's number and waits quietly for the connection.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Tomorrow morning is your D-Day. I hope you won't let me down."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Andrew is keeping watch in a corner. His previous watch shifts haven't ended well.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Hello? I guess it's you guys. Any progress on the Harting matter? I'm packing up to catch a flight to Frankfurt tonight."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "One piece of bad news and one piece of good news, boss."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Tell me the good one first. You've had enough bad news lately..."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "The good news is, we found something proving Brant is involved. We've pretty much figured out the whole story behind the document theft."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Spit it out! No time for games now!"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "There's a magic that can extract a person's soul and stuff it into another body. Developed by Professor Govich. Both Govich and Brant were subjects of the experiment. The one in Govich's body now is Heim, that Joseph Heim."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Joseph Heim? Who? Is he as famous as Adolf Hitler that you think I'd know the name?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "He was a Nazi SS mage..." David had to brief the boss on all the clues.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "So you're saying Brant's soul has been replaced?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hans Henkel Landa, former head of Section IV-E of the Nazi Security Service."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Turner was uncharacteristically silent for a moment. "I see. Well, at least it's not Adolf Hitler."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Let's hope he's thoroughly dead."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "A high-level investigation team from headquarters, including me, will arrive in Frankfurt tonight. Go directly to the Consulate General tomorrow at 9 AM. Someone will take you to meet the team and confront Brant. If what you say is true, just recite that spell in front of everyone, and the truth will be out."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Understood, boss."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Good luck to you."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: David let out a long sigh. "The boss wants us at the Consulate General tomorrow at 9 AM to meet the investigation team and confront Brant."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "How do we get there... We don't even have a place to stay tonight."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "There's a chance. If the boss's info isn't reliable, then we really can't count on going back."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "This is our chance to clear our names. But tonight, we might still run into trouble."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "So our mission is to keep the evidence safe and survive the night."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "We've done something earth-shattering. Now we can't rely on anyone, only ourselves." Andrew lowered his head, his gaze falling on a manhole cover in front of him.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: David's eyes followed Andrew's to the manhole cover.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "There's also a map in the safe house."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Maybe we can emerge from a sewer outlet near the consulate..."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Hide in the sewers for a night? Might be a good idea."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "They probably won't expect us to be in the sewers. And if they do chase us, it's easier to hide down there."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Allison crouched down and tried to move the manhole cover.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: David helped lift it.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The cycle of fate is like shackles, and are you now betting on the elusive one?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: With everyone's combined effort, you moved the manhole cover and endured a night in the sewer.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Otherwise, let's tell the boss, tomorrow we'll go up from the sewer, so people don't kick us down like rats."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "The boss is probably already on a plane by now."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Alright, then let's give him a surprise."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: On the morning of July 7th, following Turner's instructions, you arrived at the British Consulate General in Frankfurt. The previously gloomy weather had completely cleared, now with a clear sky and brilliant sunshine, hopefully a good omen. After the consulate guards verified your identities, they led you to an empty conference room on the third floor and, as a gesture of goodwill, did not confiscate your weapons.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Allison sits down in the chair and looks around to see what important figures have come today.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: So Andrew gets a seat too. Andrew's spirits have improved slightly.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Wow."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Shortly after, the conference room door opened again, and seven people entered: the leader was an elderly white male, his hair gray but still thick, meticulously combed back with a slightly fluffy feel; his face was full of wrinkles, his eyes severely drooping but still sharp; and your section chief Turner was at the end, like a small follower. They sat in a row at the "judges' bench."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: When will the boss be able to sit in the middle, so that we can also rise to prominence.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: But this leader did not sit down first; instead, he helped the even older-looking man beside him to sit in the center.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: David is full of confidence about this confrontation.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Allison leans back in the chair, waiting for the trial to begin.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: After the three parties were seated, the leader slowly spoke first, "Some of you may not have met me yet. Let me introduce myself. I am the MI6 Director. You may call me by my codename, Chief."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Andrew's eyes light up. He respectfully looks at these old men sitting on the platform. Leadership!

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Coincidentally, you," he looks at you, the corner of his mouth curling into an almost imperceptible smile, "happen to have in your possession a spell that can reveal this fact."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Andrew decides to demonstrate what he has learned in this courtroom, hoping it will work.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "It's not a coincidence; we specifically investigated this kind of magic, risking our lives to obtain this spell."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "This soul-transferring magic is called the Blessing Spell. Paired with the Blessing Spell is a Retrospection Spell. When recited in front of the body that had its soul transferred, a black mark will appear on its face." David speaks slowly, staring intently at Brant.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Brant lowers his head, avoiding your gaze.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "We got a book from the Frankfurt mystic and collector, Maxen Manson. He's probably still desperately looking for it now. This spell was also obtained from the book."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Preposterous!" he spat out the word disdainfully.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "This book is in Russian, a genuine antique. Although we haven't tested it, we believe if we perform it correctly, it should produce the effects recorded in the book."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Recite the spell.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Andrew begins trying to recite the spell according to the book's instructions.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The moment you finish reciting the spell, beneath Brant's pale face, it seems as if black worms are wriggling, gradually surfacing to form a black mark, exactly like the record in the Museum.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Chief, please look."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Chief, this is exactly the same as recorded in this book."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "This is not an accusation specifically against Brant; the other two replaced persons are Govich and Rilke. Brant once received treatment at Govich's clinic; that's probably when he was replaced. We have files discovered from Govich's clinic."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The boss leaned over and whispered something to the elderly man beside him. Immediately, the old man looked at Station Chief Brant and asked him, "Brant, no, sir, at least please state your identity yourself?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: David quietly watched his performance. This has nothing to do with us rookies.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Allison shrugged. Justice in the spy industry? Who's the real rookie here?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: As soon as Brant finished speaking, sure enough, with a "bang," the conference room door opened. As he said, two U.S. military police walked in and stood on either side behind him. He provocatively looked at the "judgment seat," and the "boss" nodded expressionlessly. Seeing the "boss's" tacit approval, Brant straightened his collar, stood up, winked at you mockingly, and said, "This is reality, everyone... Goodbye, perhaps never to meet again."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Andrew just wants to go home and eat stew. Nazis or not, he doesn't really care.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: He walked toward the door, humming an unpleasant tune, with two American military police following behind him.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Staring very displeased at this old geezer, with a murderous glint in the eyes.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Andrew looked at his boss Turner with pride and, at the same time, some shame.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: He walked very slowly, giving everyone the middle finger as he went.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: David breathed a sigh of relief, examining the expressions of each leader one by one.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "So that's the kind of relationship we have with our cousin," Allison glanced at Turner. "If we'd known, we might as well have cooperated with them."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: David looked around to see if there was anything that could serve as Hans Landa's future resting place?

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Andrew's thoughts had already drifted to the stew pot in the cafeteria. The fake Brant had been exposed, so he could go home.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Draw a gun, aim at Brant's head, and pull the trigger.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Almost simultaneously with Labinski firing, other agents in the conference room also drew their guns and aimed at you.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Andrew was startled by the sudden turn of events.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Labinski hit Brant. He fell backward, like a broken marionette, and collapsed onto the floor with a thud. Blood spread across the carpet like a deep red river, slowly and irreversibly swallowing his once extremely arrogant face.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: David seemed stunned.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Do you know the consequences of doing this?" the boss asked Labinski in a gentle tone.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Looking satisfied as Brant fell, then engaging the safety and letting go, allowing the pistol to drop to the ground, raising both hands high.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Will we also become CIA intelligence assets?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I don't know what will happen next. Perhaps this young man will be detained, interrogated, convicted. But at this moment, I only know:—he did a damn fine job." C walked over and patted your shoulder.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Now we should still have time to catch Rilke."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Also, there's a man named Adolf Müller in the sanatorium."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Yes, that person is highly likely a higher-level Nazi leader."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "If Donovan himself came to ask for him, everyone might still give him some face. Unfortunately, the old man passed away two years ago."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: David also respectfully saw the leaders off as they left.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: As soon as Turner and the others left, he deflated like a punctured ball, heavily sitting down in the chairman's seat as if he himself had been sitting in the judgment seat just moments before. He took off his glasses, rubbed his reddened nose bridge, and let out a long sigh.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Somewhat stiffly and formally performed the etiquette.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: After the leaders left, smiling at Turner: "Boss, if it weren't for your safe house, we'd be done for this time."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Boss!" David also looked grateful.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Damn... I've been defending you guys like crazy these past few days, almost got arrested as an accomplice." He looked up and glared at you, his tone half-serious, half-joking. "You guys... are real fucking jinxes."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Boss, let's go home. I'll cook you some good dishes, just learned them, they're delicious!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: He clicked his tongue, put his feet on the table, crossed his arms, and leaned back in his chair. "I thought the daily routine of the Logistics Department was just chasing smugglers, filling out forms, occasionally playing nice with gangs. Then you show up, Brant gets his head blown off, headquarters almost splits, and you drag out something like 'soul replacement'... Do you guys really have KGB backing you?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "What headquarters almost splitting?" David pricked up his ears.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: As soon as he finished speaking, he suddenly paused, stared at you, and lowered his voice a bit: "But seriously, if you really are Soviets, I won't waste words, I'll fucking pull my gun and shoot you right now."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Boss, you've worked hard! From now on, wherever you point, we'll go. If you say east, we won't go west." Answered half-jokingly, half-gratefully.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "How could I be a Soviet? You watched me grow up..."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "The Soviets must really be out of people to send four rookies like us." Alison shrugged.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Those materialists would shoot me along with God."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: He stared for a while, didn't get a retort from you, and returned to his original tone, scratching the back of his head irritably like a work dog just out of back-to-back meetings. "Forget it, forget it, stop dawdling. The documents? Mission logs, action reports, the Black Book, whatever weird stuff, hand it all over. I have to enter every single thing into the damn system for archiving."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Can we write the report at home? Boss, there's just too much, enough to write a biographical novel, more fantastical than Robinson Crusoe."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "What about the original files Harting took? And that Black Book of the Old World."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: @player2 "Boss, my action of taking out Brant just now won't be considered Soviet espionage, right?" Joked with Turner.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "The original files to be retrieved were stolen by Harting. They weren't found at his residence or hideout. According to our investigation, they might have already been sent back to his organization."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "The Black Book of the Old World is here." Takes out the Black Book of the Old World and places it on the table.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: David also took out the small mirror.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Don't know if Manson is dead or not."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Small fry. Talk to me when you've killed John F. Kennedy."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Anyway, even if he's not dead, we're not giving it back. What goes into the mouth doesn't come out." David muttered.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "What's this little mirror for? Grooming?" Harting fiddled with his hair in the mirror.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "We originally guessed Harting might be a Soviet spy, but he also seemed a bit like an Israeli spy."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Looking quite haggard."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Of course, we can't rule out local forces in West Germany either..."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Harting's organization, according to our speculation, should be Mossad."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hey, I just felt this thing in my pocket, meant to return it to Alison."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "When we were wanted, we relied on this thing to change our faces and hide." Alison took the mirror and tidied her hair.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Takes out Gutovich's three personal files.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Alright, alright, put away unrelated items."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Andrew pulled out a pistol from his pocket.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "A spy serving Mossad, codename Kant, suspected to have a grudge against Dr. Heim, the head of Odessa. It is speculated that his family members may have been in Sachsenhausen concentration camp."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: After the sound of pen tip scratching against paper, Turner wrote the final conclusion for the person "Arthur Harting".

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "During a mission last year to hunt down Nazi remnants, Harting suspected he discovered Heim's trail, but Mossad rejected Harting's request to hunt Heim. He thus chose to betray the organization and seek revenge alone."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: The end, flowers scattered.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: The end, flowers scattered.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: The end, flowers scattered.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You did not rely on the protection of any foreign powers. You did not join the CIA's special service network, nor did you hide in the shadows of the KGB. You relied on yourselves, digging out the truth inch by inch from the mire, using blood and intuition to tear open the curtain of lies.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Can we resign? This job is really tough.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I once thought it would all end at the hearing. We cleared our names, killed that damned traitor—it should be over, right?
